newsitem.title: UK: Britain may pardon executed World War One soldiers.
newsitem.headline: Britain may pardon executed World War One soldiers.

text.p: Britain may offer a posthumous pardon to more than 300 soldiers executed in World War One for cowardice and desertion.

Armed Forces Minister John Reid told the Independent newspaper on Tuesday that he was re-examing their cases in the light of strong evidence that many of the shell-shocked men were suffering from mental illnesses like post-traumatic stress disorder.
Soldiers as young as 19 were executed during the bloody trench warfare between 1914 and 1918 after cursory court martials that at times lasted just 20 minutes.
A 26-year-old soldier was shot for cowardice although he had spent five months in hospital recovering from shell-shock.
Andrew Mackinlay, a member of the Labour party that won a landslide victory in the May 1 election, has tabled a parliamentary motion calling for pardons. He has the support of most lawmakers.
"The vast majority of the 307 executed were as patriotic and brave as their million other compatriots who perished in the conflict," he told The Independent.
"Time, compassion and justice dictate that all these soldiers should now be treated as victims of the conflict," he said
